question.problem:
Find $k$ given that the vectors $a=⟨k,k,2⟩$, $b=⟨1,3,0⟩$, and $c=⟨0,4,5⟩$ are coplanar.

$k=${{field-1}}
question.worked_solution:
Computing the triple product, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}a\cdot (b\times c) & =|\begin{aligned}k & k & 2 \\ 1 & 3 & 0 \\ 0 & 4 & 5\end{aligned}| \\  & =k\cdot |\begin{aligned}3 & 0 \\ 4 & 5\end{aligned}|-k\cdot |\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 5\end{aligned}|+2\cdot |\begin{aligned}1 & 3 \\ 0 & 4\end{aligned}| \\  & =k(3\cdot 5-0\cdot 4)-k(1\cdot 5-0\cdot 0)+2(1\cdot 4-3\cdot 0) \\  & =k(15)-k(5)+2(4) \\  & =15k-5k+8 \\  & =10k+8\end{aligned}
$$

Three vectors are coplanar if and only if their triple product is zero:

$$
\begin{aligned}a\cdot (b\times c) & =0 \\ 10k+8 & =0 \\ 10k & =-8 \\ k & =-\frac{4}{5}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the three vectors are coplanar if and only if $k=-\frac{4}{5}.$
